## 4.4. Toxicology

## 4.4.1. Single-dose toxicity

No dedicated single dose toxicity study was conducted with VRVg. However, the non-clinical safety after a single administration was evaluated as part of the corresponding repeated dose toxicity studies.

## 4.4.2. Repeat-dose toxicity

Two repeated-dose toxicity studies were submitted testing two different formulations of VRVg, i.e. VRVg-1, and the commercially intended formulation VRVg-2.

The repeat-dose toxicity study VRG.RDrb08/11 evaluated local tolerance and systemic toxicity of VRVg-1 in rabbits after six IM doses over 43 days, followed by 2- or 14-day observation. Endpoints included clinical signs, body weight, food intake, ophthalmology, clinical pathology, organ weights, and histopathology of major organs per WHO guidelines. No unscheduled deaths, systemic toxicity, or vaccine-related local reactions were observed; minor injection-site changes (hematoma, oedema, erythema) occurred in both control and treated groups and were deemed unrelated to the vaccine. Histopathology revealed only slight, variable follicular hyperplasia in spleen and mesenteric lymph nodes, consistent with immune stimulation and considered pharmacologically related. All vaccinated rabbits developed anti-rabies IgG, confirming immunogenicity.

Study SP0087 RD1602 evaluated local tolerance and systemic toxicity of VRVg-2 in rabbits after six IM doses over 43 days, followed by 2- or 15-day observation. Endpoints included clinical signs, body weight, food intake, body temperature, ophthalmology, clinical pathology, organ weights, and histopathology per WHO guidelines. No unscheduled deaths, systemic toxicity, or vaccine-related local reactions were observed. Body weight, food intake, and temperature remained unaffected. Clinical pathology showed only transient fibrinogen increases, which normalized by recovery. All vaccinated rabbits developed anti-rabies IgG. Pathology revealed no macroscopic findings. Some deviations in mean organ weights (ovary, uterus, testis) were reported in vaccinated animals. The deviations observed in mean organ weight are considered incidental. Histopathology at Day 45 showed mild muscle inflammation/necrosis at the last injection site and increased cellularity in draining lymph nodes, consistent with local reaction and immune response. These changes were fully recovered by Day 58. Overall, repeated dosing induced an immune response with only minor, reversible local and lymphoid changes, and no severe findings.

## 4.4.3. Genotoxicity

VRVg vaccine is biological in nature, and as such, it is considered not to have a genotoxicity potential. Therefore, no in vitro nor in vivo genotoxicity tests were considered necessary.

## 4.4.4. Carcinogenicity

In view of the short-term exposure to VRVg and also as VRVg was considered to have no genotoxic potential, no carcinogenicity studies were performed. This is in accordance with WHO guidelines on non-clinical evaluation of vaccines.

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

## 4.4.5. Developmental and reproductive toxicity

Study VRG.DVrb08/12 evaluated the effects of the VRVg-1 rabies vaccine on pre- and post-natal development, including teratogenicity, in female rabbits. Two groups of 52 rabbits received either saline or the vaccine via IM injections (8 doses: 3 before mating and 5 during gestation). The design aimed to mimic worst-case human exposure and ensure high antibody levels during organogenesis. Rabbits were split into two sub-groups: one underwent caesarean section on day 29 for embryotoxicity assessment, and the other was allowed to litter and was observed until weaning (day 35). The study assessed maternal health, reproductive performance, and pre- and post-natal development in rabbits after eight intramuscular doses of VRVg-1 vaccine. Endpoints included maternal clinical condition, body weight, food consumption, local reactions, ovary weights, and necropsy findings, as well as foetal parameters (weight, sex ratio, external/internal abnormalities, skeletal and soft tissue examinations), as well as endpoints focussing on offspring development (survival, growth, physical and behavioural development). Blood analysis confirmed strong maternal IgG responses and efficient antibody transfer to foetuses and pups. No treatment-related adverse effects were reported. There were no signs of systemic toxicity, no impact on fertility, gestation, or lactation, and no teratogenic effects or malformations. Pup survival, growth, and development did not reveal adverse effects, and necropsy showed no vaccine-related lesions in dams or offspring. Overall, no teratogenic effects, malformations, or treatment-related anomalies were detected. Repeated VRVg-1 vaccination showed no toxicity or negative impact on reproduction or offspring development and was well tolerated. The Applicant further provided a brief justification, why it is considered acceptable not to conduct additional DART studies using the intended clinical formulation VRVg-2. As already noticed within one of the national scientific advice received during the development phase, generally, and in accordance with effective guidance on vaccine development, reproductive toxicity testing should be performed with the intended commercial formulation, i.e. VRVg-2 product, to be registered and marketed, unless a rationale can be built to justify that there is no need to generate this data with VRVg-2. An appropriate rational should be based on the comparability exercise (bridging in RDT provided), and past (clinical) experience with similar vaccines, e.g. Verorab and Cell Culture Purified Rabies Vaccine. Such data must be provided in a comprehensive manner as part of the justification for not conducting VRVg-2 dedicated DART studies within the dossier. The Applicant's

rationale for not conducting dedicated DART studies using VRVg-2 were based on four arguments:

- The previous DART study with VRVg-1 (similar formulation) using a worst-case regimen of 8 human doses showed no maternal toxicity, embryo-fetotoxicity, or adverse effects on pups.
- The repeated-dose toxicity study with VRVg-2 demonstrated good tolerance after six IM doses, even with higher protein content and rHA included in the final formulation.
- The vaccine is inactivated and adjuvant-free, reducing theoretical risk during pregnancy or lactation; clinical data, including accidental use in pregnancy and studies with related vaccines showed no safety concerns, no malformations, and normal infant development.
- Variability in glycoprotein content and potency among rabies vaccines supports that human dose levels already used in pregnant women overlap with those intended for VRVg-2, providing

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

additional reassurance.

## 4.4.6. Toxicokinetics and exposure margins

Not applicable.

## 4.4.7. Local tolerance

Local tolerance of VRVg was assessed as part of the conducted repeated-dose toxicity studies (using both, VRVg-1 and VRVg-2) in rabbits. Investigation included injection sites, gross pathology, and histopathology per WHO guidelines. No dedicated local tolerance study was performed, but repeated IM administrations showed only commonly seen, mild injection-site reactions expectable for vaccines, with no adverse findings reported. Both formulations demonstrated acceptable local tolerance profiles for IM administration.

Although ID administration is clinically intended for VRVg-2, this route of administration was not specifically tested in nonclinical studies. It was neither part of RDT studies, nor separately tested for local tolerance.

## 4.4.8. Other toxicity studies

The differences in formulation between VRVg-1 and VRVg-2 consist of an increase in antigen content as well as the addition of rHA as an excipient. rHA is fully characterized and is equivalent to native HAS for its primary, secondary and tertiary structure as well as its binding capacity. There are no biological differences between rHA and HAS. The selected rHA for the VRVg formulation has a high level of protein purity (≥99%). No safety concerns have been identified from available preclinical and clinical data. Furthermore, rHA was qualified as an excipient of VRVg-2 used in the repeated dose toxicity study conducted with VRVg-2.

## 4.4.9. Ecotoxicity/environmental risk assessment

The active substance is a natural substance, the use of which will not alter the concentration or distribution of the substance in the environment. Therefore, rabies virus (inactivated) strain WISTAR (PM/WI38 1503-3M) is not expected to pose a risk to the environment.

## 4.5. Overall discussion and conclusions on non-clinical aspects

## 4.5.1. Discussion

## Pharmacology

The pharmacology programme demonstrated that VRVg induces rabies-specific binding and neutralising antibodies across the tested animal models. The available data also support comparability between the tested VRVg batches and the licensed comparator Verorab.

The individual study designs and results are described in section 3.1.1 and are not repeated here. The exclusion of some datasets from statistical comparisons because of an absent dose-response relationship was not fully supported, as this may reflect response saturation. Nevertheless, considering the totality of the pharmacology data, this limitation does not raise a concern regarding VRVg immunogenicity or manufacturing-process comparability.

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

No dedicated secondary pharmacology, safety pharmacology, or pharmacodynamic drug-interaction studies were provided by the Applicant. This is acceptable.

## Toxicology

The repeat-dose toxicity studies with VRVg-1 and the intended formulation VRVg-2 identified no severe vaccine-related adverse effects. Findings were limited to expected immune stimulation and mild, reversible local or lymphoid changes.

The higher antigen content in VRVg-2 is not considered to introduce a new mechanism of systemic toxicity. The repeat-dose study with VRVg-2 provides direct bridging for the final formulation, including the increased antigen content.

The addition of recombinant human albumin is adequately supported by its characterisation and by the absence of new adverse findings in the GLP repeat-dose toxicity study with VRVg-2. On this basis, the formulation changes do not indicate a need for additional non-clinical toxicity studies.

The absence of a dedicated DART study with VRVg-2 is acceptable based on the negative VRVg-1 DART study, the bridging repeat-dose data with VRVg-2, the nature of the formulation changes and the available clinical experience. This risk-based conclusion is also consistent with avoiding unnecessary animal testing. This would also be in line with regulatory framework following a risk-based approach and in alignment with the principles of the 3Rs to avoid unnecessary animal testing. Lack of dedicated DART studies with VRVg-2 is moreover accordingly depicted under sections 4.6 and 5.3 in the SmPC.

The intended ID route was not assessed non-clinically. As clinical studies with VRVg-2 directly evaluated intradermal administration and reported acceptable local tolerance, an additional non-clinical local-tolerance study is not considered informative or necessary.

The absence of genotoxicity and carcinogenicity studies is acceptable given the biological nature of the vaccine, the short exposure and the applicable vaccine guidance.

## 4.5.2. Conclusions

The non-clinical pharmacology data support the immunogenicity of VRVg and do not identify a pharmacological concern. The limitations of the study package do not preclude approval, as confirmation of vaccine efficacy is primarily provided by the clinical programme. The toxicity programme, including repeat-dose studies with VRVg-1 and VRVg-2 and a DART study with VRVg-1, did not identify severe vaccine-related adverse effects. The justification for not conducting a dedicated VRVg-2 DART study is acceptable, and no additional non-clinical studies are considered necessary.

Overall, the non-clinical data is considered acceptable.

## 5.2. Clinical pharmacology

## 5.2.1. Bioanalytical methods

RVNA in human serum were quantified using a RFFIT. The GCI RFFIT method was used in the main VRVg-2 studies (VRV09, VRV11, VRV12, VRV13 and VRV14); an earlier RFFIT method was used during development of VRVg-1. The assessment focuses on the GCI method used for the intended formulation.

In short, serial dilutions of the test serum are incubated with a fixed amount of rabies virus. After incubation, susceptible BHK-21 cells are added, allowing any non-neutralized virus to infect the cells. Following a further incubation period, the cells are stained with a fluorescent anti-rabies antibody and examined under a fluorescence microscope. The highest serum dilution that prevents 50% of fluorescent foci (infected cells) is calculated using the Reed-Muench method, and results are expressed in International Units per millilitre (IU/mL) by comparison to a reference standard.

The GCI RFFIT is a functional neutralisation assay. It was validated for its intended use, including precision, accuracy/linearity, dilutability, specificity and matrix effects, with an LLOQ of 0.2 IU/mL. Supplemental validation established handling of high-titre samples and supported an upper quantification range above 900 IU/mL. Stability, robustness and study-performance information were subsequently included in the dossier. The submitted information supports the suitability of the assay for quantifying RVNA in the clinical programme.

## 5.2.2. Pharmacokinetics

In accordance with the EMA \"Guideline on clinical evaluation of vaccines\", no PK studies were conducted with VRVg-2. This is acceptable because PK evaluation is generally not applicable to vaccines, in accordance with the guideline on clinical evaluation of vaccines.

## 5.2.3. Pharmacodynamics

The PD effect of VRVg-2 is characterised by the vaccine-induced immune response. The relevant immunogenicity results are presented and assessed in the clinical efficacy section and are therefore not repeated here.

## 5.2.3.1. Mechanism of action

The vaccine induces production of RVNA. A threshold of RVNA titre of at least 0.5 IU/mL is considered as an adequate immune response after vaccination, as per WHO recommendation. RVNA are directed against the surface G glycoprotein. They exert their protective function by blocking domains of the viral glycoprotein surface required for the attachment of the virus to susceptible cells.

Neutralization of rabies virus by the various Ig isotypes, IgM and IgG, has been considered as a basis of effective protection in animals and humans against death from rabies virus infections (Katz ISS et al., Arch Virol., 2017).

Vaccination is highly effective at preventing disease when administered before or shortly after exposure to virus. Follow-up studies carried out with other rabies vaccines than VRVg have shown that the immune response can persist for up to 10 years after vaccination and passive transfer studies suggest that it is IgG that provides the most effective protection against the disease (Strady A et al., J Infect Dis., 1998).

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

## 5.2.4. Overall discussion and conclusions on clinical pharmacology

## 5.2.4.1. Discussion

The GCI RFFIT method used in the main VRVg-2 studies was adequately validated according to ICH Q2 (R1). A conservative ULOQ of &gt;900 IU/mL was established. Based on the submitted validation reports, it is agreed that the rabies-virus RFFIT assay as conducted at GCI was suitable for its intended use to detect and quantitate the levels of RVNA in human serum samples.

The specificity conclusion, particularly regarding the high variability observed in ED50 titers when heterologous competitors were used, was addressed and explained by the Applicant. Furthermore, the Applicant explained how samples with titers exceeding 900 IU/mL will be handled.

## 5.2.4.2. Conclusions

Overall, the clinical pharmacology package is acceptable. The RFFIT assay, used to measure RVNA titers in human serum as a surrogate for vaccine immunogenicity, is deemed suitable for its intended purpose.

## 5.3. Clinical efficacy

## 5.3.1. Dose response study

## 5.3.1.1. Study VRV11 - Immunogenicity and Safety of a Purified Vero Rabies Vaccine - Serum Free when administered according to a Simulated Rabies Post-Exposure Regimen in Healthy Adults

## 5.3.1.1.1. Study design and methods

VRV11 was a multicenter, observer-blind, controlled, randomized, Phase II study. A total of 320 subjects aged 18 to &lt; 65 years were to be included. Each subject was to receive one of the 2 formulations of the VRVg or the Human Diploid Cell Vaccine Imovax Rabies. Vaccination was to be performed according to the ESSEN postexposure schedule (i.e., a total of 5 injections [1 injection per day] administered at D0, D3, D7, D14 and D28) and HRIG were to be administered at D0.

Subjects were to be assigned to the VRVg-2 groups (low, medium and high dose), VRVg-1 group or Imovax Rabies vaccine group with a 2:2:2:1:1 allocation ratio (n= 80 or 40 subjects, respectively).

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

Table 6: Targeted quantity of Ag at final product stage in VRVg-1 and VRVg-2 dosages (low, medium and high doses)

| Formulation and dosage   | Targeted Ag quantity at labeled product stage   |
|--------------------------|-------------------------------------------------|
| VRVg-1                   | 4.5 IU/dose                                     |
| VRVg-2 Low dose          | 4.5 IU/dose                                     |
| VRVg-2 Medium dose       | 6.6 IU/dose                                     |
| VRVg-2 High dose         | 9.0 IU/dose                                     |

Abbreviations: Ag, antigen; FBP, final bulk product; IU, international units.

All subjects were to provide blood samples before the first vaccination at D0 (baseline titer) and at D14, D28, D42 and at M7 for the assessment of the immune response to the rabies vaccine.

Safety was to be assessed in all subjects during the vaccination period and up to 28 days after vaccinations, in terms of occurrence of AEs, SAEs and AESIs. In addition, SAEs and AESIs were to be collected up to 6 months after the last vaccination in all subjects.

Since Imovax Rabies vaccine can be visually distinguished from VRVg-1 and VRVg-2, to avoid bias in safety data collection, the person who assessed the safety was different from the person who administered the vaccine (blind observer).

## HRIG (Imogam Rabies):

A 5-mL syringe was used and filled using several vials as necessary. The content of the syringe was to be injected by IM route at a body site distant from the rabies vaccine injection site (anterolateral thigh). A maximum of 5 mL was to be administered by injection; the total volume was to be divided and administered at separate sites (sites had to be at least 3 cm apart). HRIG was calculated based on subject body weight (see table below).

## 5.3.1.1.2. Objectives and endpoints

## Immunogenicity

## Objectives

To describe the immune response induced by VRVg-2 (low, medium and high dose) versus VRVg-1 and Imovax Rabies vaccine at Day D14 (7 days after the third injection), at D28 (14 days after the fourth injection), at D42 (14 days after the last injection), and at M7 (6 months after the last injection).

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

## Endpoints

- Titers (IU/mL) summarized at the subject/timepoint level.
- o RVNA titers against rabies virus obtained by the RFFIT at D0, D14, D28, D42 and M7 in all subjects;
- o Subject with an RVNA titer ≥ 0.5 IU/mL at D0, D14, D28, D42 and M7;
- o Subject with an RVNA titer ≥ lower limit of quantitation (LLOQ) IU/mL, at D0, D14, D28, D42 and M7;
- o Individual titer ratio: D14/D0, D28/D0, D42/D0 and M7/D0.
- Virus neutralization: complete or incomplete, summarized at the subject/timepoint level.
- o Subject with complete neutralization at the starting dilution (1/5) of the RFFIT assay at each timepoint.

## Safety

## Objectives

To describe the clinical safety profile of VRVg-2 (low, medium and high dose) versus VRVg-1 and Imovax Rabies vaccine after each vaccine injection.

## Endpoints

The endpoints for the evaluation of safety were:

- Occurrence of any unsolicited systemic AEs reported in the 30 minutes after each vaccine injection.

## Collection of Injection Site Reactions

- Occurrence of solicited (prelisted in the subject's DC and CRF) injection site reactions occurring within 7 days after each injection;
- Occurrence of unsolicited (spontaneously reported) injection site reactions occurring within 28 days after each injection.

## Collection of Systemic Reactions and Adverse Events

- Occurrence of solicited (prelisted in the subject's DC and CRF) systemic reactions between the first and the second injections as well as between the second and the third injections, and up to 7 days after the remaining injections;
- Occurrence of unsolicited (spontaneously reported) systemic AEs between each injection and up to 28 days after the last injection;
- Occurrence of SAEs throughout the trial.

## 5.3.2. Main studies

5.3.2.1. VRV12 - Immunogenicity and Safety of a Purified Vero Rabies Vaccine - Serum Free in Comparison with Verorab and Imovax Rabies, in a Pre-exposure Regimen in Both Paediatric and Adult Populations and a Single Booster Dose of Purified Vero Rabies Vaccine - Serum Free Administered at 1 Year Post-3-Dose Primary Series, and Between 2 up to 3 Years Post-One Week 2-Dose Primary Series in a Subset of Adults in Thailand

## 5.3.2.1.1. Study design

This was a controlled, randomized, multi-centre (4 centres that enrolled subjects in Thailand) study with Primary Series of either a 3-dose PrEP regimen or 2-dose PrEP regimens of VRVg-2 or comparators, followed by a Booster Phase (in a subset of adult population) using a single dose of VRVg-2 regardless of the vaccine received in the Primary Series.

## Primary Series

Subjects were planned to be vaccinated in Primary Series according to a 3-dose schedule PrEP regimen (Primary Series Cohort 1) or a 2-dose PrEP regimen (Primary Series Cohort 2). Cohort 1 was planned to be composed of paediatric and adult subjects randomized according to a 3:1:1 ratio (VRVg-2: Verorab: Imovax Rabies) composing Groups 1, 2, and 3, respectively. Cohort 2 was planned to be composed of adult subjects randomized according to the same 3:1:1 ratio composing Groups 4, 5, and 6, respectively. Primary Series for both cohorts were planned to be observer-blinded.

## Booster Phase

Two subsets of adult subjects were planned to be randomized at enrollment to be part of the Booster Phase:

An adult subset from Cohort 1 and hereafter referred as \"Booster Phase Cohort 1\" was planned to be conducted in a blinded manner. Subjects were planned to receive a booster dose of VRVg-2 one year after the 1st vaccine injection in the Primary Series (including blood samples collection pre-booster at M12 and post-booster at M12+D14), regardless of what type of rabies vaccine was used in Primary Series.

An adult subset from Cohort 2 and hereafter referred as \"Immunogenicity Persistence and Booster Phase Cohort 2\" was planned to be followed-up for evaluation of immunogenicity persistence after Primary Series (including blood samples collection at M6, M12, M18, and pre-booster between M24 up to M36) and to receive a booster dose of VRVg-2 between M24 up to M36 (including blood samples collection at M24 up to M36+D14), regardless of what type of rabies vaccine was used in Primary Series.

The randomization and vaccination during the Primary Series and Booster Phase for Cohort 1 were planned to be conducted in a blinded manner. Similarly, for Cohort 2, randomization and vaccination from the enrollment up to V04 (28 days after the last vaccination in the Primary Series) were planned to be conducted in a blinded manner. The booster dose vaccination in the Immunogenicity Persistence and Booster Phase Cohort 2 was planned to be conducted in an open-label manner with a new batch of VRVg-2; as a reminder, the laboratory analysts remained blinded during the whole study.

A total of 1700 healthy subjects were planned to be enrolled: 505 paediatric subjects and 505 adults in Primary Series Cohort 1, and 690 adults in Primary Series Cohort 2.

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

A subset of 170 adult subjects in Cohort 1 (Booster Phase Cohort 1) were planned to receive a booster dose of VRVg-2 after 1 year (M12) regardless of the vaccine used in the Primary Series.

A subset of 230 adult subjects in Cohort 2 (Immunogenicity Persistence and Booster Phase Cohort 2) were planned to receive a booster dose of VRVg-2 between 2 up to 3 years (M24-M36) regardless of the vaccine used in the Primary Series.

## Visits and phone calls (PC)

## Primary Series

For paediatric subjects and adults who were planned to receive the 3-dose PrEP regimen (Primary Series Cohort 1), a total of 5 visits (V01 to V05) and 1 PC were planned.

For adult subjects who were planned to receive 2-dose PrEP regimen (Primary Series Cohort 2), a total of 4 visits (V01 to V04) and 1 PC were planned.

## Booster Phase

Booster Phase Cohort 1: for the Primary Series 3-dose PrEP regimen + Booster Phase, a total of 8 visits (V01 to V08) and 2 PCs were planned.

Immunogenicity Persistence and Booster Phase Cohort 2: for the Primary Series 2-dose PrEP regimen + immunogenicity persistence + Booster Phase, a total of 10 visits (V01 to V10) and 1 PC are planned.

## Vaccination

Paediatric subjects (505 subjects) and adult subjects (505 subjects) in Primary Series Cohort 1 were planned to receive a total of 3 injections at D0, D7, and D28 through IM route. Adult subjects in Primary Series Cohort 2 (690 subjects) were planned to receive a total of 2 injections at D0 and D7 through IM route.

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

A subset of 170 adult subjects in Cohort 1 (Booster Phase Cohort 1) were planned to receive a booster dose of VRVg-2 after 1 year (M12) of the 1st injection regardless of the vaccine used in the Primary Series and a subset of 230 adult subjects in Cohort 2 (Immunogenicity Persistence and Booster Phase Cohort 2) is planned to receive a booster dose of VRVg-2 between 2 up to 3 years (M24-M36) after the 1st injection regardless of the vaccine used in the Primary Series.

## Duration of study participation

For Primary Series Cohort 1, the duration of each subject's participation in the study was approximately 7 months (28 day-vaccination period followed by 6-month safety follow-up period). For the subset of adult subjects in Booster Phase Cohort 1 who received a single booster dose of VRVg-2 (1 booster dose 365 days after Primary Series followed by 6-month safety follow-up period), the duration was approximately 18 months. For Primary Series Cohort 2, the duration of each subject's participation in the study was approximately 7 months (1 week vaccination period followed by 6-month safety follow-up period). For the subset of adult subjects in Immunogenicity Persistence and Booster Phase Cohort 2 who was followed up for evaluation of immunogenicity persistence after Primary Series (including blood samples collection at M6, M12, M18, and pre-booster between 24 up to 36 months) and who received a single booster dose of VRVg-2 (after the blood sample collection between 24 up to 36 months), the duration was approximately 30 to 42 months.

## Blood sampling

Paediatric subjects and adult subjects (Primary Series Cohort 1) were planned to provide 3 blood samples: at D0 (prior to the 1st vaccine injection), at D28 (21 days after the 2nd vaccine injection), and at D42 (14 days after the 3rd vaccine injection). Adult subjects in Primary Series Cohort 2 were planned to provide 2 blood samples: at D0 (prior to the 1st vaccine injection) and D28 (21 days after the 2nd dose vaccine injection). The subset of adults who were planned to be part of the Booster Phase Cohort 1 had 2 additional blood samples in the Booster Phase: at M12 (prior to the booster dose) and M12+D14 (14 days after booster dose), to evaluate immunogenicity in the Booster Phase. The subset of adults who were planned to be part of the Immunogenicity Persistence and Booster Phase Cohort 2 had 5 additional blood samples: at M6, M12, M18, pre-booster between M24 up to M36 to evaluate immunogenicity persistence after the Primary Series, and at post-booster between M24 up to M36+14D to evaluate immunogenicity after booster.

## Treatment

Investigational Product: VRVg-2 VRVg-2 (theoretical targeted Ag content at final product stage = 9 IU/dose) was the single VRVg-2 dosage used. The dose selected for the present study was based upon results obtained in VRV11 study (Phase II dose ranging study). Control Product 1: Verorab (purified inactivated rabies vaccine prepared on Vero cell line) Verorab was administered according to the recommendations described in the package insert of the licensed vaccine. Control Product 2: Imovax Rabies (purified inactivated rabies vaccine prepared on human diploid cell cultures)

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

Imovax Rabies was administered according to the recommendations described in the package insert of the licensed vaccine.

## Randomisation and blinding

The primary series was observer-blinded for both Cohort 1 (3-dose pre-exposure prophylaxis [PrEP] regimen) and Cohort 2 (one week 2-dose PrEP regimen). Specifically, in addition to the subjects, health care providers, data collectors, outcome assessors, and Sponsor personnel (e.g., clinician, data managers, biostatistician) were to remain blinded until the 1st statistical analysis (note that the vaccine administrators were unblinded). The laboratory analysts who were involved in the blood sample testing were to remain blinded during the whole study. Both cohorts included paediatric and adult participants, and randomization was conducted in a 3:1:1 ratio (VRVg-2: Verorab Rabies: Imovax Rabies) by permutated block randomization, stratified by centre and age group. Two subsets of adult subjects were also randomized at enrolment to be part of the booster phases: an observer-blind conducted Booster Phase Cohort 1 included participants from Cohort 1 to receive a booster dose of VRVg-2 one year after the first vaccine injection of the primary series regardless of what type of vaccination was received in the primary series, and a Booster Phase Cohort 2 included participants from Cohort 2 for evaluation of immunogenicity persistence and for administration of a booster dose of VRVg-2 between M24 and M36, regardless and not blinded to what type of rabies vaccine was used in the primary series. The randomization ratio of the primary series was planned to be maintained as best possible in these booster cohorts. The blind was permitted to be broken for a specific subject by the investigator in the event of an AE or by the GPV department through an internal system for reporting to health authorities in the case of an SAE as described in ICH E2A, in both cases only when the identification of the vaccine received could have influenced the treatment of the subject. Otherwise, it was to be upheld until the end of 6-month safety follow-up after booster phase in Cohort 1 and up to D35 of the primary series in Cohort 2. Randomisation listings were created independently for Cohorts 1 and 2 at D0(V01) though an IRT

system.

## Study population

Healthy male and female subjects ≥ 1 year of age (i.e., from the day of the 1 st birthday onwards, with no upper age limit) on the day of inclusion who never received any vaccination against rabies (in preor post-exposure regimen), who were not bitten by, or exposed to a potentially rabid animal in the previous 6 months, and who were not at high risk for rabies exposure during the study.

## 5.3.2.1.2. Objectives and estimands

## Primary objective

## Immunogenicity

- To demonstrate that VRVg-2 was non-inferior to Verorab and Imovax Rabies vaccines in each age group (paediatric and adult populations) when administered as a 3-dose PrEP regimen, in terms of proportion of subjects achieving an RVNA titer ≥ 0.5 IU/mL at D42, i.e., 14 days after the 3 rd injection (for Primary Series Cohort 1).

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

## Primary Endpoint

The primary endpoint for the evaluation of immunogenicity is:

- RVNA titers (IU/mL) measured by the RFFIT at D42 for paediatrics and adults in Primary Series Cohort 1
- o Subject with an RVNA titer ≥ 0.5 IU/mL at D42

## Estimands for the primary objective

The Applicant did not specifically define an estimand for the primary objective. They target the estimate of the difference in the proportion of protocol-adhering subjects with an RVNA titer ≥ 0.5 between the VRVg-2 vaccination group and the Verorab and Imovax vaccination groups at D42 in both adult and paediatric participants when the vaccines are administered in a 3-dose PrEP regimen in order to test that VRVg-2 is non-inferior in evoked immune response.

## Statistical methods for estimation and sensitivity analysis on primary estimands

Analysis Sets The FAS was defined as the subset of randomized subjects who received at least one dose of the study vaccine during the primary series, and the FASI was the subset of those who additionally had a baseline RVNA titre lower than 0.5 IU/mL. The FASP was defined as the subset of randomized subjects from Cohort 2 who received a complete primary rabies vaccination series (i.e., one week 2-dose PrEP regimen in this case) and had at least one valid post-vaccination serology result, and the FASI for Immunogenicity Persistence (FASIP) was defined as the subset of FASP subjects who additionally had a baseline titre lower than 0.5 IU/mL. The FAS for the booster series were defined as those participants from Cohort 1 (ie, the 3-dose PrEP regimen) who received a booster at M12 (FASB1) and those participants from Cohort 2 (i.e the 2-dose PrEP regimen); in both cases a complete primary rabies vaccination series was required. The respective FASI (B1/B2) sets included those participants that additionally had a baseline titre lower than 0.5 IU/mL. PPASs were defined as those subsets of the respective FAS at time points D28 and D42 of the primary series, and at the time points M12 and at M24 up to M36 of the booster series, who could be considered fully adhering to the protocol. Participants who were seropositive at D0 or experienced relevant protocol deviations before the time point of the set definition, such as ones relating to inclusion/exclusion/withdrawal criteria, improper preparation and administration of the allocated vaccine, deviations from the planned vaccination or sampling windows, missing or invalid serology tests, and intake of prohibited medication were thereby excluded. The SafAS and Safety Analysis Set for Booster (SafASB) were defined respectively as the subset of subjects having received at least one dose of the corresponding series (primary/booster); their vaccination group was considered determined by the vaccination actually received in (first dose of) the primary series. The immunogenicity data was planned to be analysed on the PPAS for D42 and D28 outcomes primarily, and on the FAS and the FASI as supplementary analyses if the difference between number of subjects in the PPAS and number of subjects in the FAS was not less than 10%. The immunogenicity persistence data for adult subset subjects was analysed descriptively on the FASIP, the FASP, as well as on the PPAS for the booster series.

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

The immunogenicity data for the booster subjects were to be analysed on the FASB1/B2, FASIB1/B2, and the PPAS for the booster series (overall and according to the vaccine randomized in the primary series).

The safety analyses were to be based on the SafAS and the SafASB. Statistical Methods - Primary Endpoint

In each age group of the primary series Cohort 1, the immunogenicity of VRVg-2 was compared to that of the Verorab and Imovax rabies vaccines at D42, i.e., 14 days after the 3rd vaccine injection, using NI testing. Specifically, the difference in the proportion of subjects with an RVNA titer ≥ 0.5 IU/mL at D42 between the VRVg-2 group and each of the two comparator groups was tested based on the twosided 95% CI calculated using the Wilson score method without continuity correction: the primary objective of NI was considered demonstrated if the lower limit of the 95% CI of the difference of the proportions (VRVg-2 minus comparator) was greater than -5% for both comparisons in both age groups (paediatric and adult).

## Missing Data Handling

Since few missing data were anticipated no imputation was planned or carried out.

## Secondary objectives

## Safety

- 1.To describe the safety profile of VRVg-2 versus Verorab and Imovax Rabies vaccines, after each vaccine injection, in each age group (for Cohort 1 and Cohort 2);
2. To describe the safety of a single booster dose of VRVg-2 among the subsets of adults following Primary Series of 3-dose Primary Series in addition to booster dose at M12 (for Booster Phase Cohort 1);
3. To describe the safety of a single booster dose of VRVg-2 among the subsets of adults following one week 2-dose Primary Series in addition to booster dose between M24 up to M36 (for Immunogenicity Persistence and Booster Phase Cohort 2).

## Immunogenicity

1. To demonstrate that the observed proportion of subjects in the VRVg-2 group (overall) achieving an RVNA titer ≥ 0.5 IU/mL at D42 was at least 99%, with a lower limit of the 95% CI of at least 97% (for Primary Series Cohort 1), only if the primary objective is achieved;
2. To demonstrate that VRVg-2 was non-inferior to Verorab and Imovax Rabies vaccines in each age group (paediatric and adult populations), in terms of proportion of subjects achieving an RVNA titer ≥ 0.5 IU/mL at D28, i.e., 21 days after the 2nd injection (for pooled Primary Series Cohort 1 and Cohort 2), only if the 1st secondary immunogenicity objective is achieved;
3. To demonstrate that 2-dose VRVg-2 at D28 was non-inferior to 3-dose Imovax Rabies at D42 in each age group (paediatric and adult populations, respectively), in terms of proportion of subjects achieving an RVNA titer ≥ 0.5 IU/mL, only if the 2nd secondary immunogenicity objective is achieved;
4. To demonstrate that the observed proportion of subjects in the VRVg-2 group (overall) achieving an RVNA titer ≥ 0.5 IU/mL at D28 was at least 99%, with a lower limit of the 95% CI

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

- of at least 97% (for pooled Primary Series Cohort 1 and Cohort 2), only if the 3 rd secondary immunogenicity objective is achieved;
5. To demonstrate that 2-dose Imovax Rabies at D28 was non-inferior to 3-dose Imovax Rabies at D42 in the overall subjects (pooled paediatric and adult subjects) in Cohort 1, in terms of proportion of subjects achieving an RVNA titer ≥ 0.5 IU/mL, only if the 4 th secondary immunogenicity objective is achieved;
6. To describe the immune response induced by VRVg-2 versus Verorab and Imovax Rabies vaccines at D28 (i.e., 21 days after the 2nd injection), and at D42 (i.e., 14 days after the 3 rd injection) in all age groups (paediatric and adult populations);
7. To describe the immune response induced by VRVg-2 at D14 after a single booster dose of VRVg-2 administered at month M12 after the Primary Series with VRVg-2, Verorab, or Imovax Rabies vaccines in the subset of adult subjects (for Booster Phase Cohort 1);
8. To describe persistence of the immune response at M6, M12, M18, and pre-booster between M24 up to M36 post Primary Series vaccination in the subset of adults who were randomized to receive a booster and completed the 2-dose vaccination in the Primary Series (for Immunogenicity Persistence and Booster Phase Cohort 2);
9. To describe the immune response induced by VRVg-2 at D14 after a single booster dose of VRVg-2 administered between M24 up to M36 after the Primary Series with VRVg-2, Verorab, or Imovax Rabies vaccines in the subset of adult subjects who were randomized to receive a booster and completed the 2-dose vaccination in the Primary Series (for Immunogenicity Persistence and Booster Phase Cohort 2).

## Estimands for the secondary objectives

As for the primary objective/endpoint, the Applicant did not specifically formulate an estimand for any of the secondary endpoints.

## Statistical methods for estimation and sensitivity analysis on the secondary estimands

Secondary hypotheses testing was to be considered only if the primary objective was met, and in that case secondary objectives were to be evaluated sequentially (as below), i.e. following the fixedsequence method: Superiority in the VRVg-2 group at D42: Demonstrated if the observed proportion of subjects with an RVNA titer ≥ 0.5 IU/mL at D42 in VRVg-2 group is at least 99.0%, and the lower limit of the 95% CI of the overall observed proportion of (adult and paediatric) subjects in the VRVg-2 group in Cohort 1 with an RVNA titer ≥ 0.5 IU/mL at D42 was at higher than or equal to 97% as calculated using the exact binomial distribution (Clopper Pearson method). NI in the 2-dose VRVg-2 group versus the 2-dose Verorab and Imovax rabies groups at D28: Demonstrated based on the same approach as the primary analysis, only VRVg-2 was tested against both comparator vaccines at D28 in each age group using pooled primary series Cohort 1 and Cohort 2 data for adult subjects. NI in the 2-dose VRVg-2 group at D28 versus the 3-dose Imovax rabies group at D42: Demonstrated based on the same approach as the primary analysis, only the NI boundary was specified to be -10% (-5% as a supplementary analysis) and adult subjects from Cohort 1 and 2 were pooled. Superiority in the VRVg-2 group at D28 (added in Protocol amendment 5 while the study was ongoing): Demonstrated based on the same approach as the secondary superiority objective testing procedure at D42, only VRVg-2 is tested against both comparator groups at D28 for each using pooled primary series Cohort 1 and Cohort 2 data in both age groups.

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

NI in the 2-dose Imovax rabies group at D28 versus the 3-dose Imovax rabies group at D42 (added in Protocol amendment 5 while the study was ongoing): Demonstrated if the lower limit of the two-sided 95% CI of the difference of the 2 proportions, as calculated using a generalized linear model (GLM) for binomial responses, is greater than -10% (-5% as a supplementary analysis) in each age group from Cohort 1 only.

All further secondary endpoints were analysed descriptively by age group and vaccine group: geometric means/mean ratios and corresponding 95%CIs for titres/ratios, exact binomial distribution estimates (Clopper Pearson method) for single proportions, and reverse cumulative distribution curves were planned where appropriate.

## 5.3.2.1.3. Results

## Participant flow and numbers analysed

## Study dates

Study initiation date: 21 October 2019 (first subject first visit). A total of 1708 subjects were enrolled and randomized in the study between 21 October 2019 and 11 February 2020.

Interim CSR Version 1.0: 11 Dec 2023

Final data report date: 24 April 2025 (last contact for 6-month follow-up of Booster Phase in Cohort 2)

The analyses presented in the CSR (final CSR Version 2.0, dated 11 Aug 2025) are based on a database lock date of 03 June 2025.

## Disposition of participants

Overall, the number of subjects enrolled and randomized in centre 7640003 was higher (898 subjects) than in centres 7640001 (200 subjects), 7640002 (405 subjects), and 7640004 (205 subjects). Indeed, study site 7640003 was the only centre that continued to recruit for Cohort 2 subjects, as planned in the protocol. The proportion of subjects enrolled and randomized in each treatment group was consistent with the 3:1:1 randomization ratio.

At study centre level, no paediatric subjects were enrolled in centre 7640001. All the subjects randomized to Cohort 2 were enrolled in centre 7640003.

## Deviations from study plan

All changes in study conduct were implemented via protocol amendments.

Protocol v8.0 dated 12 June 2023 was used in the study. There were five numbered protocol amendments between these versions in total, the following changes were not purely administrative:

- Amendment 2: Adjustment of the estimation of seroconversion rate at D28 for adults subjects in VRVg-2 and the control vaccines from 99% to 96.5%. Incorporation of a single booster between 2 and up to 3 years with a new batch of VRVg-2 as per new guidelines.
- Amendment 3: Addition of a secondary objective to demonstrate the acceptability of the immune response at D28 of a 1-week 2-dose PrEP regimen. Addition of the evaluation of persistence of the immune response at M6, M12, M18 and pre-booster between M24 up to M36 after a 2-dose primary series in the subset of adults who are randomized to be part of the Immunogenicity Persistence and Booster Phase Cohort 2.
- Amendment 4: Addition of the statement that subjects with RVNA titers &lt; 0.5 IU/mL at all timepoints may be offered an additional injection of a local licensed rabies vaccine chosen by the Investigator. Measured added to minimize subjects' withdrawal due to missing visits (at M6, M12, and/or M18) during the Immunogenicity Persistence and Booster. Clarification of the IRT randomisation scheme.
- Amendment 5: Addition of two secondary immunogenicity objectives (the last two in the formal testing hierarchy). Adjustment of the attrition rate estimation.

## Protocol Deviations

- During the whole study - Randomized subjects

Overall, among the 1708 randomized subjects, a total of 255 subjects (14.9%) presented at least 1 major or critical protocol deviation: 63 subjects (10.4%) in Group 1, 25 subjects (12.3%) in Group 2, 21 subjects (10.5%) in Group 3, 86 subjects (20.5%) in Group 4, 31 subjects (22.3%) in Group 5, and 29 subjects (20.9%) in Group 6.

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

## - Primary Series (Cohorts 1 and 2) - Randomized subjects

Among the 1708 randomized subjects, a total of 206 subjects (12.1%) presented at least 1 major or critical protocol deviation in the primary series: 54 subjects (8.9%) in Group 1, 23 subjects (11.3%) in Group 2, 15 subjects (7.5%) in Group 3, 67 subjects (16.0) in Group 4, 24 subjects (17.3%) in Group 5, and 23 subjects (16.5%) in Group 6. Among them 101 (5.9%) subjects had a deviation related to randomization procedure (60 subjects [14.3%] in Group 4, 21 subjects [15.1%] in Group 5, and 20 subjects [14.4%] in Group 6).

A total of 23 subjects (1.3%) reported at least 1 critical protocol deviation in the primary series: 19 subjects (1.1%) received earlier rabies vaccination, 2 subjects (0.1%) were pregnant, 1 subject (&lt; 0.1%) had an invalid ICF, and 1 subject (&lt; 0.1%) participated or planned to participate in another study.

A total of 5 subjects (0.3%) presented at least 1 major or critical protocol deviation due to COVID-19 pandemic situation in the Primary Series: 3 subjects (0.5%) in Group 1, 1 subject (0.5%) in Group 2, and 1 subject (0.7%) in Group 5.

## - Booster Phase for Cohort 1 - Randomized subjects for booster

Among the 170 randomized subjects for booster in Cohort 1, a total of 28 subjects presented at least 1 major or critical protocol deviation in the Booster Phase: 17 subjects (16.7%) in Group 1, 5 subjects (14.3%) in Group 2, and 6 subjects (18.2%) in Group 3. The most frequently reported major protocol deviations were due to planned sample not performed after Visit 1 (9 subjects in Group 1, 4 subjects in Group 2, and 1 subject in Group 3).

No critical protocol deviation was reported during the Booster Phase in all groups of Cohort 1.

Among the 170 randomized subjects for booster in Cohort 1, a total of 10 subjects presented at least 1 major or critical protocol deviation due to COVID-19 pandemic situation in the Booster Phase: 8 subjects (7.8%) in Group 1, 1 subject (2.9%) in Group 2, and 1 subject (3.0%) in Group 3. The most frequently reported protocol deviations were due to IMP not administered and planned sample not performed within the protocol-specified time window (Visit 06).

## - Immunogenicity Persistence and Booster Phase for Cohort 2 - Randomized subjects for booster

Among the 230 randomized subjects for booster in Cohort 2, a total of 23 subjects presented at least 1 major or critical protocol deviation during the immunogenicity persistence period: 11 subjects (8.0%) in Group 4, 6 subjects (13.0%) in Group 5, and 6 subjects (13.0%) in Group 6. The most frequently reported major protocol deviations were due to planned sample not performed after Visit 1 (6 subjects in Group 4, 3 subjects in Group 5, and 4 subjects in Group 6).

Among the 230 randomized subjects for booster in Cohort 2, a total of 23 subjects presented at least 1 major or critical protocol deviation in the Booster Phase: 14 subjects (10.1%) in Group 4, 6 subjects (13.0%) in Group 5, and 3 subjects (6.5%) in Group 6. The most frequently reported major protocol deviations were due to planned sample not performed after Visit 1 (11 subjects in Group 4, 5 subjects in Group 5, and 3 subjects in Group 6) and to the non-administration of the IMP (10 subjects in Group 4, 5 subjects in Group 5, and 3 subjects in Group 6).

No critical protocol deviation was reported during the immunogenicity persistence period and the Booster Phase in all groups of Cohort 2.

No subjects in Cohort 2 were impacted by COVID-19 pandemic situation in the Booster Phase.

5.3.2.2. VRV13 - Immunogenicity and Safety of a Purified Vero Rabies Vaccine - Serum Free in Comparison with Verorab and Imovax Rabies, in a Simulated Rabies Post-Exposure Regimen in Healthy Adults in France

## 5.3.2.2.1. Study design

This was a modified double-blind (Groups 1 to 3) and open for Group 4, controlled, randomized, multicentre (2 sites in France) study.

A total of 636 healthy adults (≥ 18 years of age) were planned to be enrolled. Randomization ratio was 3:1:1:1 (VRVg-2 + HRIG: Verorab vaccine + HRIG: Imovax Rabies vaccine + HRIG: VRVg-2).

- Group 1: VRVg-2 + HRIG at D0 n=318
- Group 2: Verorab vaccine + HRIG at D0 n=106
- Group 3: Imovax Rabies vaccine + HRIG at D0 n=106
- Group 4: VRVg-2 n=106

## Visits and phone calls

A total of 7 visits (Visit [V]01-V07) and 1 phone call (for the 6-month safety follow up) were planned.

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

## Vaccination

All subjects were to receive a total of 5 injections: at D0, D3, D7, D14, and D28 through intramuscular (IM) route.

In addition, HRIG were concomitantly administered at D0 to subjects randomized to Groups 1 to 3.

## Blood sampling

All subjects were to provide 4 blood samples: at D0 (prior to the first vaccine injection), at D14 (7 days after the third vaccine injection), at D28 (14 days after the fourth vaccine injection), and at D42 (14 days after the fifth vaccine injection).

## Treatment

## Study Product: VRVg-2

VRVg-2 (theoretical targeted Ag content at final product stage = 9 IU/dose) was the single VRVg-2 dosage used. The dose selected for the present study was based upon results obtained in VRV11 study (Phase II dose ranging study).

## Control Product 1: Verorab Vaccine

Verorab was administered according to the recommendations described in the package insert of the licensed vaccine.

## Control Product 2: Imovax Rabies Vaccine

Imovax Rabies was administered according to the recommendations described in the package insert of the licensed vaccine.

Other Product: IMOGAM Rabies-HT licensed HRIG was administered at D0 in all subjects

- Human rabies immunoglobulins at least 150 IU/mL

Preparation and Administration, Dose Selection and Timing

Imogam Rabies-HT was injected as recommended in the package insert and as approved in the marketing authorization of the product. As this study was performed in a simulated post-exposure condition, the entire volume was administered by IM route. The volume to be injected per subject was to be calculated based on the body weight (20 IU/kg) as presented in the figure below:

## Randomisation and blinding

Randomization of participants was performed centrally using an IRT. The randomisation ratio was planned to be 3:1:1:1 to the following vaccination groups: VRVg-2 + HRIG, Verorab vaccine +HRIG, Imovax Rabies vaccine + HRIG, and VRV-g2, and also to be stratified by centre (permutated block randomisation).

The study was planned to be conducted in a modified double-blind manner for vaccination groups 1 to 3 above: the subject, the Investigator, and study staff members who collected the safety data and laboratory personnel who analysed the blood samples were all to be blinded to the group assignment while the staff member preparing and administering the vaccination was unblinded. Group 4, which received only VRVg-2, was open-label.

The blind was permitted to be broken for a specific subject by the investigator in the event of an AE or by the GPV department through an internal system for reporting to health authorities in the case of an SAE as described in ICH E2A, in both cases only when the identification of the vaccine received could have influenced the treatment of the subject. The code was ultimately planned to be broken for the primary analysis, but the randomization list was not to be provided to Investigators and kept until the end of the study (finalization of the CSR).

## Study population

The study population included healthy male and female subjects ≥ 18 years of age on the day of inclusion.

## 5.3.2.2.2. Objectives and estimands

## Primary objective

## Immunogenicity

- To demonstrate that VRVg-2 is non-inferior to Verorab and Imovax Rabies vaccines when coadministered with HRIG, in terms of proportion of subjects achieving a RVNA titer ≥ 0.5 IU/mL at D28, i.e., 14 days after the fourth vaccine injection.

## Estimands for the primary objective

The Applicant did not specifically define an estimand. They target an estimate for the difference in the proportion of protocol-adhering subjects with an RVNA titer ≥ 0.5 to test whether it is non-inferior in the VRVg-2 +HRIG group compared to both the Verorab +HRIG and Imovax +HRIG groups at D28 when the vaccines are administered according to a four-vaccination ESSEN regimen. The comparison to the group receiving VRV12 remains descriptive.

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

## Statistical methods for estimation and sensitivity analysis on primary estimands

Analysis Sets The FAS was defined as the subset of randomized subjects who received at least one dose of the study vaccines, and the FASI was defined as a subset of participants from the FAS who have a baseline RVNA titer lower than 0.5 IU/mL. The PPAS is a subset of the FAS that was defined at D28 (the timepoint used for primary objective assessment) by excluding participants with relevant protocol deviations before that time point, such as ones relating to inclusion/exclusion/withdrawal criteria or being seropositive at D0, improper preparation and administration of the allocated vaccine and HRIG, deviations from the planned vaccination or sampling windows, missing or invalid serology tests, and intake of prohibited medication. The primary and key secondary immunogenicity endpoints were planned to be evaluated on the PPAS, with analyses on the FAS(I) serving as supplementary analyses. The SafAS was defined for each vaccination dose as the subset of subjects having received this dose. All subjects were analysed according to the study vaccine they actually received (at the first dose). Safety data recorded for a vaccine received out of the protocol design were to be excluded from the analysis (and listed separately). Note: · If one subject received both VRVg-2 vaccine and HRIG at first dose, the vaccination group for safety analysis is Group 1; · If one subject received Verorab vaccine or Imovax Rabies vaccine at first dose, no matter whether HRIG was concomitantly administered or not, the vaccination group for safety analysis is Group 2 or Group 3; · If one subject received VRVg-2 vaccine only at first dose, the vaccination group for safety analysis is Group 4; · If one subject received HRIG only at first dose, the vaccination group for safety analysis is \"Other\" and will be excluded from safety analysis. Statistical Methods - Primary Endpoint The immunogenicity of VRVg-2 +HRIG was compared to that of the Verorab +HRIG and Imovax rabies + rabies + HRIG vaccines at D28, i.e., 14 days after the 4 th vaccine injection, using NI testing. Specifically, the difference in the proportion of subjects with an RVNA titer ≥ 0.5 IU/mL at D28 between the VRVg-2 group and each of the two comparator groups was tested based on the two-sided 95% CI calculated using the Wilson score method without continuity correction: the primary objective of NI was considered demonstrated if the lower limit of the 95% CI of the difference of the proportions (VRVg-2 minus comparator) was greater than -5% for both comparisons. Missing Data Handling Since few missing data were anticipated no imputation was planned or carried out. Sensitivity Analyses To evaluate the possible impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the study conduct, the following sensitivity analyses were planned to be performed:

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

· Impact of COVID-19 pandemic on subject's disposition, based on enrolled subjects Note: Subjects impacted by COVID-19 pandemic situation corresponded to subjects with at least one major/critical protocol deviation due to COVID-19, or who did not complete the study due to COVID-19, or who reported an impact on 6-month follow up in pandemic form · Impact of COVID-19 pandemic on immunogenicity analysis, based on FASI. · Impact of medical history of suspected/confirmed COVID-19 pandemic before enrolment on immunogenicity analysis, based on FASI. · Impact of the use of concomitant medications that are used during the study/ or were used not over 2 months before enrolment for treating/preventing COVID-19 (i.e., Hydroxychloroquine and chloroquine) on immunogenicity based on FASI. · Immunogenicity of subjects who did not take any concomitant medications for treating/preventing COVID-19 (i.e., Hydroxychloroquine and chloroquine) within 2 months before enrollment based on PPAS · Impact of COVID-19 pandemic on safety overview up to 28 days after any vaccination, based on SafAS. · Impact of medical history of suspected/confirmed COVID-19 before enrollment on safety overview up to 28 days after any vaccination, based on SafAS. · Impact of the use of concomitant medications that are used during the study/ or were used at least 2 months before enrollment for treating/preventing COVID-19 (i.e., Hydroxychloroquine and chloroquine) on safety overview up to 28 days after any vaccination, based on SafAS. Note: If only few subjects were impacted by COVID-19 (&lt;5% in randomized subjects), only the

corresponding listings will be provided instead of tables for immunogenicity and safety evaluation.

## Secondary objectives Safety

- To describe the safety profile of VRVg-2 versus Verorab and Imovax Rabies vaccines when coadministered with HRIG, as well as that of VRVg-2, after each vaccine injection.

## Immunogenicity

- To demonstrate that the proportion of subjects in the VRVg-2 + HRIG group achieving an RVNA titer ≥ 0.5 IU/mL at D28 is at least 95%;
- To describe the immune response induced by VRVg-2 versus Verorab and Imovax Rabies vaccines when co-administered with HRIG, as well as that induced by VRVg-2, at D14 (7 days after the third injection), at D28 (14 days after the fourth injection), and at D42 (14 days after the last injection).

## Estimands for the secondary objectives

As for the primary objective/endpoint, the Applicant did not define any estimands.

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

## Statistical methods for estimation and sensitivity analysis on the secondary estimands

Secondary hypotheses testing was to be considered only if the primary objective was met, i.e., a gatekeeping approach to Type I error control was foreseen. One secondary endpoint was formally tested: Superiority in the VRVg-2+HRIG group at D28: Demonstrated if the lower limit of the 95% CI of the proportion, calculated using the exact binomial distribution (Clopper Pearson method), was equal to or higher than 95%.

All other secondary endpoints were planned to be evaluated descriptively by vaccine group.

## 5.3.2.2.3. Results

## Participant flow and numbers analysed

## Study dates

Study initiation date: 01 July 2019 (first subject first visit). Last subject last visit (without additional procedures for 2 subjects): 19 January 2021 Last subject last visit (with additional procedures for 2 subjects): 04 July 2022 Last subject last contact (i.e., 6-month safety follow-up, without additional procedures for 2 subjects): 01 July 2021 Study period (first subject first visit to last subject last contact without additional procedures for 2 subjects): 01 July 2019 to 01 July 2021 Vaccination period (Visit 1 to Visit 5): 01 July 2019 to 22 December 2020 Active Phase (Visit 1 to Visit 7): 01 July 2019 to 19 January 2021. The analyses presented in the CSR (final clinical study report (CSR) version 1.0, dated 05 October

2022) are based on a database lock date of 03 September 2021.

## Disposition of participants

A total of 640 subjects were randomized (252 [39.4%] subjects in Centre 2500001 and 388 [60.6%] subjects in Centre 2500002). The numbers of randomized subjects were 320 subjects in Group 1, 107 subjects in Group 2, 107 subjects in Group 3, and 106 subjects in Group 4. Two subjects were randomized to Group 4 (VRVg-2) but actually received the vaccination schedule of Group 1 (VRVg-2 + HRIG).

A total of 594 randomized subjects (92.8%) completed the active phase (295 [92.2%] subjects in Group 1, 102 [95.3%] subjects in Group 2, 97 [90.7%] subjects in Group 3, and 100 [94.3%] subjects in Group 4).

A total of 46 (7.2%) randomized subjects had early study termination from the active phase (25 [7.8%] subjects in Group 1, 5 [4.7%] subjects in Group 2, 10 [9.3%] subjects in Group 3, and 6 [5.7%] subjects in Group 4). The main reason for early study termination was protocol deviation in 40 subjects (21 [6.6%] subjects in Group 1, 4 [3.7%] subjects in Group 2, 10 [9.3%] subjects in Group 3, and 5 [4.7%] subjects in Group 4). The remaining 6 subjects were withdrawn as per subject decision (3 [0.9%] subjects in Group 1 and 1 [0.9%] subject in Group 4), lost to follow-up (1 [0.9%] subject in Group 2) and AE (1 [0.3%] subject in Group 1).

## Deviations from study plan

Final protocol is version 7.0 dated 14 Mar 2022. The following amendments are listed:

- Amendment 1 (dated 27 September 2019): Study hold due to a severe SAE, all subjects who were participating in the study had to be informed about the related SAEs in the ICF or through an addendum to the ICF, targeted sample size for enrolment increased.
- Amendment 2 (dated 27 April 2020): Study hold due to increase in COVID cases in France. Type of follow-up replaced where possible, targeted sample size for enrolment increased.
- Amendment 3 (dated 09 March 2021): Addition that subjects with no or delayed immune was to be offered additional blood tests to evaluate a potential immunosuppression, and that vaccination with a licensed vaccine in the country may be offered after assessment.

5.3.2.3. VRV00014 - Immunogenicity and Safety of the Purified Vero Rabies Vaccine - Serum Free (VRVg) Using the Zagreb Regimen as Simulated Rabies Post-Exposure Prophylaxis in Healthy Adults in Thailand

## 5.3.2.3.1. Study design

This was a randomized, observer-blind, controlled, multi-centre (3 centres in Thailand) study.

A total of 201 healthy adult subjects (≥ 18 years old without upper age limit on the day of inclusion) were planned to be enrolled and randomized. The randomization ratio was 2:1 (VRVg-2:Verorab).

- Group 1: VRVg-2 + HRIG at D0 N=134
- Group 2: Verorab + HRIG at D0 N=67

## Visits and phone calls

A total of 7 visits ([V]01-V07) and 1 phone call were planned.

## Vaccination

All subjects were to receive a total of 3 doses of rabies vaccine (including 4 injections) as follows: 2 injections at D0 (V01), 1 injection at D7 (V02), and 1 injection at D21 (V04). All vaccinations were to be given through IM route.

At V01, the 2 injections were to be done on different arms. In addition, HRIG was to be concomitantly injected at D0 to all subjects, in both Group 1 and Group 2.

## Blood sampling

All subjects were to provide 4 blood samples: at D0 (prior to vaccination [VAC]1), at D14 (7 days after VAC2; V03), at D35 (14 days after VAC3; V05), and at D90 (up to 3 months after VAC1; V07). Blood sampling was to be done prior to vaccination and prior to HRIG injection at D0. Each blood sample volume drawn from subjects was to be 6 mL.

## Treatment

## Study Product: VRVg-2

VRVg-2 (theoretical targeted antigen content at final product stage=9 IU/dose) was the single VRVg-2 dosage used. The dose selected for the present study was based upon results obtained in VRV11 study (Phase II dose-ranging study).

## Control Product: Verorab

Verorab vaccine was administered according to the recommendations described in the package insert of the licensed vaccine.

## Other Product: Imogam

The recommended dose was 20 IU/kg (or 9 IU/lb) of body weight.

Preparation and Administration, Dose Selection and Timing

Imogam Rabies-HT was injected as recommended in the package insert and as approved in the marketing authorization of the product. As this study was performed in a simulated post-exposure condition, the entire volume was administered by IM route. The volume to be injected per subject was to be calculated based on the body weight (20 IU/kg) as presented in the figure below:

|   Weight (kg) |   Quantity of HRIG (nr) |   Volume (mL) |   Number of injections |
|---------------|-------------------------|---------------|------------------------|
|            60 |                    1200 |             8 |                      2 |
|            80 |                    1600 |         10.67 |                      3 |
|           100 |                    2000 |         13.33 |                      3 |
|           120 |                    2400 |            16 |                      4 |

## Study population

The study included healthy male and female subjects ≥ 18 years old without upper age limit on the day of inclusion. For detailed inclusion and exclusion criteria, see study protocol.

## 5.3.2.3.2. Objectives

## Primary objective

## Immunogenicity

- To describe the immune response induced by VRVg-2 and Verorab vaccines at Day (D)14 and D35 when co-administered with HRIG at D0, according to the Zagreb (2-1-1) IM regimen in healthy adult subjects.

## Secondary objectives

## Safety

- Occurrence of any unsolicited systemic AEs reported in the 30 minutes after each vaccination;
- Occurrence of solicited (pre-listed in the subject's DC and eCRF) injection site and systemic reactions occurring within 7 days after each vaccination;
- Occurrence of unsolicited (spontaneously reported) injection site reactions occurring within 28 days after each vaccination and unsolicited systemic AEs/ ARs between each vaccination and up to 28 days after the last vaccination;
- Occurrence of SAEs and AESIs throughout the study (until 6 months after last vaccination).

## Immunogenicity

- RVNA titers (IU/mL) against rabies virus obtained by the RFFIT;
- Percentage of subjects with an RVNA titer ≥ 0.5 IU/mL at D90;
- Subjects with an RVNA titer ≥ LLOQ IU/mL at D90;
- Individual RVNA titer ratio: D90/D0.

5.3.2.4. VRV09 - Immunogenicity and Safety of a Purified Vero Rabies Vaccine - Serum Free (VRVg) Assessed with the Institut Pasteur du Cambodge (IPC: 2-2-2-0-0) and Thai Red Cross (TRC: 2-2-2-0-2) Intradermal Regimens as Simulated Rabies Post-Exposure Prophylaxis in Healthy Subjects in Thailand

## 5.3.2.4.1. Study design

This was a randomized, observer-blind, controlled, multi-centre (3 centres s in Thailand) study.

A total of 376 healthy subjects were planned to be enrolled: 168 paediatric subjects (≥ 1 to &lt; 18 years [84 subjects ≥ 1 to &lt; 12 years and 84 subjects ≥ 12 to &lt; 18 years]) and 208 adults (≥ 18 years without upper age limit). The randomization ratio was 2:1, (VRVg-2:Verorab) in each age group.

The overall planned adult population was 208 subjects considering:

- 40 adult subjects enrolled as per superseded protocol version 5.0 and randomly allocated in Group 3 and Group 4 who received vaccines co-administered with ERIG, but the ERIG coadministration was discontinued as per Sponsor decision
- 168 adult subjects to ensure the sample size of the study as initially planned who were enrolled and randomly allocated in Group 5 and Group 6 (as per amended protocol version 6.0) and receive vaccines co-administered with HRIG

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

| Pediatric subjects: N=168          |       |
|------------------------------------|-------|
| Group 1: VRVg-2                    | N=112 |
| Group 2: Verorab                   | N=56  |
| Adult subjects: N=208              |       |
| Group 3: VRVg-2 + ERIG at Day (D)0 | N=26  |
| Group 4: Verorab + ERIG at D0      | N=14  |
| Group 5: VRVg-2 + HRIG at D0       | N=112 |
| Group 6: Verorab + HRIG at D0      | N=56  |

## Visits and phone calls

A total of 8 visits (V) (V01-V08) and 1 phone call (for the 6-month safety follow-up) were planned.

## Vaccination

All subjects were to receive a total of 4 doses of rabies vaccine (including 8 injections) as follows: 2 injections of vaccine given at each of D0 (V01), D3 (V02), D7 (V03), and D28 (V05). At each visit, the 2 injections were to be done on each arm (one 0.1 mL injection on each arm) at different sites through ID route.

In addition, ERIG was concomitantly injected at D0 to adult subjects in both Group 3 and Group 4 (as per superseded protocol version 5.0), and HRIG was concomitantly injected at D0 to adult subjects in both Group 5 and Group 6 (as per amended protocol version 6.0). ERIG and HRIG were administered through IM route in the thighs.

## Blood sampling

All subjects were to provide 4 blood samples: at D0 (prior to VAC1), at D14 (7 days after VAC3), at D42 (14 days after VAC4), and at D90 (up to 3 months after VAC1). Blood sampling was to be done prior to vaccination and prior to ERIG (Group 3 and Group 4) or HRIG (Group 5 and Group 6) injection at D0.

## Treatment

## Study Product: VRVg-2

VRVg-2 was the single VRVg-2 dosage used. The dose selected for the present study was based upon results obtained in VRV11 study (Phase II dose ranging study).

## Control Products: Verorab

Verorab vaccine was administered according to the recommendations described in the package insert of the licensed vaccine.

## Other Product 1

Thai Red Cross (TRC) Society ERIG was administered at D0 in adult subjects enrolled as per superseded protocol version 5.0 only (Group 3 and Group 4).

Preparation and Administration, Dose Selection and Timing

ERIG at the dosage of 40 IU/kg was injected via IM route. If a large volume (&gt; 15 mL for adults) is required, it is recommended to administer this as divided doses at both sides in the thigh muscle. The immunoglobulin had to be administered away from the vaccination site.

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

TRC Society ERIG was injected as recommended in the package insert and as approved in the marketing authorization of the product. As this study was performed in a simulated post-exposure condition, the entire volume was administered by IM route.

## Other Product 2

Imogam Rabies-HT Licensed HRIGs was administered at D0 in only (Group 5 and Group 6).

Preparation and Administration, Dose Selection and Timing

Imogam Rabies-HT was injected as recommended in the package insert and as approved in the marketing authorization of the product. As this study was performed in a simulated post-exposure condition, the entire volume was administered by IM route. The volume to be injected per subject was to be calculated based on the body weight (20 IU/kg) as presented in the figure below:

Figure 14: Imogam Rabies-HT administration schemata

|   Weight (kg) |   Quantity of HRIG (nn) |   Volume (mL) |   Number of injections |
|---------------|-------------------------|---------------|------------------------|
|            60 |                    1200 |             8 |                      2 |
|            80 |                    1600 |         10.67 |                      3 |

## Study population

The study included male and female paediatric (≥ 1 to &lt; 18 years) and adult (≥ 18 years without upper age limit on the day of inclusion) subjects. For detailed inclusion and exclusion criteria, see study protocol.

## 5.3.2.4.2. Objectives

## Primary objective

## Immunogenicity

- To describe the immune response induced by VRVg-2 and Verorab vaccines at Day (D)14 (to assess the immune response after 3 doses [2-2-2]) and D42 (to assess the immune response after 4 doses [2-2-2-0-2]) when administered as standalone in healthy paediatric population or coadministered with HRIG (Group 5 and Group 6) at D0 in healthy adults.

## Secondary objectives

## Immunogenicity

- To describe the immune response induced by VRVg-2 and Verorab vaccines at D14 (to assess the immune response after 3 doses [2-2-2]) when co-administered with ERIG (Group 3 and Group 4) at D0 in healthy adults.
- To describe the immune response induced by VRVg-2 and Verorab vaccines at D90 (to assess the immune response 90 days post-rabies simulated exposure, which covers the rabies incubation period of the majority of cases) when administered as standalone in healthy

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

## Safety

- To describe the safety profile of VRVg-2 and Verorab vaccines as standalone in paediatric population or when co-administered with ERIG (Group 3 and Group 4) or HRIG (Group 5 and Group 6) at D0 in adults, after each vaccination.
