## 9. Benefit-risk assessment

## 9.1. Therapeutic context

## 9.1.1. Disease or condition, proposed therapeutic indication

Rabies is an acute viral encephalitis transmitted mainly through bites or scratches from infected animals. Once clinical symptoms develop, the disease is almost invariably fatal.

VaxRabeo is an inactivated rabies vaccine that induces rabies virus-neutralising antibodies. The proposed indication is pre-exposure and post-exposure prophylaxis against rabies in individuals of all age groups.

## 9.1.2. Available therapies and unmet medical need

There is no effective treatment for rabies. Prevention relies on pre-exposure vaccination for individuals at risk and prompt post-exposure prophylaxis. Although PrEP does not eliminate the need of PEP in case of rabies exposure, it simplifies the rabies PEP schedule since a reduced number of vaccine doses is needed and RIG is not required.

Several rabies vaccines containing inactivated rabies virus, intended for both PrEP and PEP in all age groups, are available in European countries. VaxRabeo provides an additional serum-free Vero-cellderived vaccine option for the established prophylactic regimens.

## 9.2. Main clinical studies

The pivotal studies were VRV12 and VRV13.

VRV12 was a controlled, randomised, multi-centre study to compare immunogenicity and safety of VRVg-2 to comparators Verorab and Imovax Rabies for 2-dose in adults and 3-dose intramuscular PrEP regimens in paediatric and adult participants. Booster administration of VRVg-2 at 1 year after first dose was assessed in a subset of adults who had received the 3-dose PrEP regimens, whereas booster administration of VRVg-2 at 2 to up to 3 years after first dose was investigated in a subset of adults who had received the 2-dose PrEP regimen. Antibody persistence at Month 6, 12, 18 and before the booster was only evaluated in the subset of adults who were vaccinated with the 2-dose PrEP regimen.

VRV13 was a controlled, randomised, multi-centre study to compare immunogenicity and safety of VRVg-2 with the same comparators for concerning two IM PEP regimens in adults, i.e., the 5-dose Essen regimen and the 4-dose Essen regimen, in adult subjects. To simulate the PEP aspect, participants received HRIG at Day 0, except for Group 4 (VRVg-2 only), to allow comparative evaluation of the impact of HRIG on immune responses. The study was modified double-blind (Groups 1 to 3, VRVg-2, Verorab, Imovax Rabies, respectively) and open-label for Group 4.

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

VRV00014 and VRV09 were supportive, descriptive studies of the Zagreb IM PEP regimen in adults and the IPC/TRC ID PEP regimens in paediatric and adults, respectively.

## 9.3. Favourable effects

Study VRV12 met its primary objective, demonstrating non-inferiority of VRVg-2 to Verorab and Imovax Rabies for the 3-dose IM PrEP regimen at Day 42 (14 days after the 3 rd injection) in paediatric and adult participants, using a -5% non-inferiority margin. The corresponding response proportions were 100% in both VRVg-2 age groups. Key secondary analyses supported the 2-dose IM PrEP regimen, with 100% of paediatric participants and 98.3% of adults achieving RVNA ≥ 0.5 IU/mL at Day 28 after VRVg-2. Study VRV13 (adults only) met its primary objective, demonstrating non-inferiority of VRVg-2 to Verorab, and to Imovax Rabies when co-administered with HRIG at Day 28 (i.e., 14 days after the 4 th vaccination), using a -5% margin. The response proportion with VRVg-2 + HRIG was 99.6%. Responses after the 5-dose regimen was 100% This was supported by data on immune responses induced by the Zagreb IM PEP regimen in VRV00014 (adults only). Additional support comes from data in the paediatric population (who did not receive HRIG) after the evaluated intradermal PEP regimens in VRV09. However, immune responses in study VRV09 in the adult population (who received HRIG) were substantially lower in both VRVg-2 and Verorab groups (proportion of subjects with RVNA titer ≥ 0.5 IU/mL was 59.4% vs. 51.9% at Day 14, 96.2% vs. 100% at Day 42, and 75.0% vs. 78.4% at Day 90, respectively.) In study VRV12, a VRVg-2 booster induced RVNA ≥ 0.5 IU/mL in all evaluated adult participants,

irrespective of the vaccine used for primary vaccination.

## 9.3.1. Uncertainties and limitations about favourable effects

The principal uncertainties concern indirect support for the intradermal PrEP regimen, absence of paediatric PEP data with concomitant RIG, and the unexpectedly low Day 14 responses in adults receiving the IPC intradermal PEP regimen in VRV09. No data are available for the intradermal PrEP regimen (i.e., 2 doses each at Day 0 and Day 7). The only data for ID administration derive from paediatric subjects who received VRVg-2 or Verorab in Study VRV09 (investigated TRC and IPC ID PEP regimens, two doses each on Day 0, Day 3, Day 7, and Day 28 were administered, first measurement at Day 14 [7 days after the 3 rd vaccination]) but without RIG. PEP vaccination schedules in the paediatric population were only studied with VaxRabeo/VRVg-2 without concomitant administration of RIG, as evaluation of simulated PEP conditions in this population is considered unjustified and unethical. PEP schedules with RIG are only available from the adult population. Seroprotection rates at Day 14 in adults (as PEP with concomitant HRIG) were unexpectedly low for both VRVg-2 and Verorab compared to VRVg-2 and Verorab data of IM trials, which questions the suitability of the IPC PEP regimen (and to some extent the TRC regimen). Concerning the TRC

schedule, data are also limited by a small sample size due to a high rate of protocol deviations leading to exclusion from the PPAS for Day 42. Although immune responses at Day 14 after the 4 th vaccination were generally in line with expectations (96.2% and 100% achieving ≥0.5 IU/mL in VRVg-2+HRIG and Verorab+HRIG groups), three participants failed to reach the threshold, including one below 0.2 IU/mL. RVNA GMTs were also numerically lower for VRVg-2+HRIG compared to Verorab+HRIG (3.13 (2.49; 3.92) vs. 4.41 (3.31; 5.87)), respectively).

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

This uncertainty is mitigated by restricting the IPC regimen to individuals below 18 years and by the availability of alternative adult PEP regimens. Evidence for booster use and persistence is based on adult data, and some proposed uses rely on extrapolation across age groups, routes or regimens.

## 9.4. Unfavourable effects

Across the clinical programme, 2,079 participants received at least one dose of the final VRVg-2 formulation, with safety follow-up through 6 months after the last vaccination. The pooled primaryseries safety analysis supporting SmPC section 4.8 included 1,906 VaxRabeo recipients and excluded booster-only exposure and participants who received ERIG. Solicited injection-site reactions occurred in 45.7% of VaxRabeo recipients, compared with 41.5% for Verorab and 46.0% for Imovax Rabies. Solicited systemic reactions occurred in 42.4%, 34.2% and 42.5%, respectively. Grade 3 systemic reactions were uncommon (1.7%, 0.8% and 1.0%, respectively).

The incidences of solicited ARs tended to be higher in female and younger participants.

Unsolicited AEs occurred in 23.1% of VRVg-2 recipients, compared with 20.3% for Verorab and 22.4% for Imovax Rabies; related unsolicited events occurred in 2.5%, 1.9% and 3.1%, respectively. SAEs through 6 months occurred in 1.4%, 1.6% and 1.2%, respectively. No vaccine-related SAE, death or AESI was identified for VRVg-2.

## 9.4.1. Uncertainties and limitations about unfavourable effects

The safety database is sufficient to characterise common and uncommon AEs but may not detect potential rare AEs.

Data are limited for infants &lt;24 months and participants aged &gt;65 years of age, pregnant or breastfeeding individuals, in immunocompromised individuals, and for concomitant administration with other vaccines.

## 9.6. Benefit-risk assessment and discussion

## 9.6.1. Importance of favourable and unfavourable effects

Rabies is almost invariably fatal after symptom onset, so prevention of infection is of very high clinical importance. The most important favourable effects are the robust neutralising-antibody responses demonstrated in the pivotal PrEP and Essen PEP studies, supported by additional regimens and booster data. The immunobridging approach is acceptable because RVNA ≥ 0.5 IU/mL is the established immunogenicity threshold used in the programme and comparative responses were shown against authorised rabies vaccines.

The results were robust and consistent across age groups, regimens and mode of administration. Extrapolation to regimens not specifically tested and compared in the clinical development programme is acceptable. This refers to extrapolation of data from one ID regimen to another, from PrEP to PEP regimens and across age groups.

The most important unfavourable effects are transient injection-site and systemic reactions. They were mainly mild or moderate, Grade 3 reactions were uncommon, and no vaccine-related SAE, death or AESI was identified. Reactogenicity was somewhat higher than with Verorab and similar to Imovax Rabies, with no unusual or unexpected pattern of adverse events.

## 9.6.2. Balance of benefits and risks

The benefits of VaxRabeo are the induction of protective rabies virus-neutralising antibody responses across the pivotal IM PrEP and PEP regimens, supported by additional regimen and booster data. The available immunogenicity data demonstrate that VaxRabeo/VRVg-2 elicits Rabies virus-neutralizing antibody titers, in particular protective titers, of at least the magnitude as the comparators in both paediatric and adult individuals. The safety data reveal an overall comparable reactogenicity of VaxRabeo in terms of nature, incidences and severity of solicited and unsolicited adverse reactions with the approved comparator vaccines across age groups and administration routes. The risks are clearly outweighed by the benefit of preventing fatal rabies disease.

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

## 9.7. Benefit-risk conclusions

The overall benefit/risk balance of VaxRabeo is positive.
